title: Paid ad campaign performance analysis
prompt: You are analyzing four weeks of Meta campaign data for Cedar & Coil (CSV supplied below; conversions are purchases, revenue is purchase value, frequency is average weekly impressions per person). Produce a performance analysis for the founder: (1) a per-campaign four-week summary with total spend, total conversions, CPA, and ROAS where revenue is available, showing your arithmetic for at least CPA; (2) name the best and worst performing campaign with evidence; (3) diagnose the most important week-over-week trend problem; (4) recommend one specific budget change and one bounded test to run next; (5) state the data limitation that would most change your conclusions. Note anything unusual in the data quality.

completion.check: Per-campaign four-week totals are computed and correct within rounding: Prospecting - Broad spend $4,800, 169 conversions, CPA ~$28.40; Prospecting - Small-Space Interest spend $2,400, 138 conversions, CPA ~$17.39; Retargeting - 30d Engagers spend $1,600, 83 conversions, CPA ~$19.28 (or stated over known weeks only); Launch Teaser totals acknowledge the missing week.

Small-Space Interest is identified as the best performer (lowest CPA ~$17.39, stable, ROAS ~3.9) and Broad as the biggest problem (weekly CPA rising from $20 to $48 while CTR halves from 1.8% to 0.9%); calling the Launch Teaser 'worst' on CPA alone without noting its video-views objective does not pass.
There is one specific budget change (e.g. shift spend from Broad toward Small-Space Interest) and one bounded test (what change, what metric, what timeframe or budget).

skill_adherence.check: The empty conversions/revenue cells for Launch Teaser in the week of 2026-07-20 are flagged as missing data (e.g. a tracking gap), not treated as zero or silently summed over.

Any Launch Teaser CPA or ROAS uses spend and outcomes from exactly the same complete rows, or is reported as unavailable. Dividing all four weeks of spend by only three known weeks of conversions/revenue fails.
The arithmetic behind key claims is shown (at least CPA calculations), and metric definitions/sources are used as supplied rather than invented.
A limitation that would most change the conclusion is stated (e.g. attribution window, missing week, four-week sample), and correlation is not presented as proven causation.

best_practices.check: The diagnosis is driven by week-over-week movement (Broad's CTR/CPA deterioration, Retargeting frequency climbing 6.1 to 11.4 with falling conversions), not four-week averages alone.
Recommendations are prioritized (one clear primary move) rather than an unranked laundry list.

The proposed test has one control and one changed variable, a duration or spend cap, one primary KPI, a numeric win rule, and either a numeric minimum sample or an explicit rule for declaring the result inconclusive.
